hints.title: Missing Criteria
hints.text: An employee has missing information if their record is absent in either the Employees table (no name) or the Salaries table (no salary).

hints.title: Identifying Missing IDs
hints.text: Select IDs from Employees not in Salaries, and select IDs from Salaries not in Employees.

hints.title: Combining and Sorting
hints.text: Combine both sets of IDs using union and sort the result by employee_id ascending.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT employee_id FROM Employees WHERE employee_id NOT IN (SELECT employee_id FROM Salaries)
UNION
SELECT employee_id FROM Salaries WHERE employee_id NOT IN (SELECT employee_id FROM Employees)
ORDER BY employee_id ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(E + S log(E + S)) where E is employees and S is salaries
complexity.space: O(E + S) space for combined union result
complexity.notes: Symmetric difference using UNION and subquery exclusion.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Inner joins drop both missing categories completely.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: UNION deduplicates and ordering produces the requested sorted ID sequence.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize this as symmetric difference across two tables.
